From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Subject: Performance horizon: SLO handshake & streaming constraints — post-call summary

Hi Sanjay & Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum on p95/p99 qualification and the streaming acceptance criteria you called out. Notes below are distilled from the call and prioritized asks for the POC run.

Summary of ask (from your side):
- End-to-end p95 and p99 targets for production traffic shape (UI chat + short completion flows): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 450ms.
- Streaming voice/long-turn interactions: keep tail latency below ~600ms for incremental tokens and stable under concurrency peaks.
- Sustained concurrency target across region: 250 concurrent chat sessions, burst to 800 for short windows.
- Throughput baseline: median request payload ~350 tokens, 90th percentile payload ~800 tokens, embedding calls separate.

What Redwood will validate during POC:
1) End-to-end hosted API measurements (our endpoint) against your current provider using a synthetic replay of your traffic envelope (seq length dist + concurrency).
2) Streaming handshake and incremental-token latency with WebSocket-based streaming and our delta-token batching disabled to measure worst-case tails.
3) Concurrency shaping tests: steady-state at 250 concurrent users + two burst scenarios (800 sustained for 2 minutes, 800->400 ramp).
4) KV cache warmup / cold-start behavior and recommendations for prefix caching or pinned warmup.

Immediate next steps / owners: 
- Ben (me): share the test plan and a small set of sample payloads to match your traffic by EOD Thu (attached: horizon_p95p99_test_plan.xlsx).
- Karthik: work with your infra team to set up IP allowlist + short-lived API key for the POC — target Mon 05/24.
- Camila: lead the streaming test script and provide the exact HTTP/WebSocket test harness we’ll use; will capture per-token timing.
- Aditya: define the runbook for measuring p95/p99 end-to-end (what services we instrument, where we measure — client-side vs edge vs model-serving) and include fallback gates.

Please confirm these owners and timeline or reply with corrections.

Thanks,
Ben
--
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 17:05:12 -0700

Cc: Priya Menon <priya@horizonhealth.com>
Subject: Re: Performance horizon: SLO handshake & streaming constraints — post-call summary

Ben —

Thanks for the concise recap. That matches our ask. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The p95/p99 targets are measured end-to-end from our frontend load balancer to user-visible completion (so client-side). We understand model-serving-only numbers will be lower; we need the full path.
- For streaming, we care about per-token arrival jitter (we’ll share a waveform example). If p99 for incremental tokens drifts > 350ms from expected, the UX degrades.
- We can provide a replay trace for a 24-hour window to mimic a production day.

We’ll confirm the infra contacts for IP allowlisting by tomorrow. Please include an explicit canary rollback criterion in the runbook (e.g., if p99 increases > 20% over baseline or error rate > 0.5%).

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
VP Product, Horizon Health

Quick infra note — I’ll take point on the allowlist and the POC API key. Karthik here (you saw me on the call). Action items: 
- I need Horizon's ephemeral egress IPs and the LB health-check endpoint by Friday 05/22 to configure the allowlist.
- For telemetry, we'll ask Horizon to run a lightweight agent that records client-side timestamps (send/receive) so we can compare apples-to-apples. If they cannot run the agent, we will rely on synthetic replay from a regional load generator with header-preserved timestamps.

Also adding a note for measurement boundaries: we will report p95/p99 at three slices — client-observed, edge (Redwood gateway), and model-serving. The decision to accept Hosted requires client-observed p99 to be within the agreed threshold or a documented mitigation plan.

Karthik

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Performance horizon: SLO handshake & streaming constraints — post-call summary

Attached is the initial streaming harness plan (summary tab in the spreadsheet). Key test vectors I’ll run:
- Token-size sweep: 64 / 256 / 512 / 1024 tokens to capture tail behavior.
- Concurrency profiles: 250 steady, burst to 800 for 120s, ramp down to 400 over 3 minutes.
- Network emulation: add 20–80ms RTT and 1% packet loss in a subset to emulate mobile connectivity.

I’ll push the harness (k6 + simple websocket client) to the shared drive and include per-token timing logs. Aditya — can you confirm instrumentation tags we need (edge_latency_ms, token_emit_ms, model_recv_ms, model_emit_ms)?

Camila

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya@horizonhealth.com>
Subject: Re: Performance horizon: SLO handshake & streaming constraints — post-call summary

Confirmed instrumentation tags (we’ll export these to the POC dashboard):
- client_ts (ms) — timestamp captured at the frontend before request send
- edge_recv_ts, edge_send_ts — Redwood gateway ingress/egress
- model_recv_ts, model_emit_ts — serving runtime kernel timestamps
- token_emit_ms (per-token delta when streaming)

Canary rollback criteria (suggested):
- Client-observed p99 increase > 20% relative to baseline OR
- Client-observed error rate > 0.5% OR
- Sustained p95 degradation > 40% for > 10 minutes

I’ll author a short runbook and share by COB Friday. Ben — once you confirm, I’ll include the rollback checks in the automated dashboard alerts.

Aditya

Sanjay / Priya —

Appreciate the quick confirmations. Attached test plan is the first pass (spreadsheet). Proposed schedule:
- Wed 05/26: Shadow replay with 30-minute steady-state at 250 concurrent sessions (no streaming). We’ll collect client/edge/model slices.
- Thu 05/27: Streaming smoke + token-size sweep at low concurrency to validate instrumentation.
- Fri 05/28: Full concurrency run with burst windows.

If Horizon can provide the 24-hour replay trace, we’ll use Wed/Thu to generate a synthetic regional replay that mirrors their spike patterns. Karthik — please confirm allowlist timeline; once we have it we’ll publish the ephemeral API key.

Marissa — tagging you to capture any commercial constraints (timeboxing POC, success criteria for go/no-go) and flag if we need an interim credit or SLA exception during the test window.

If no objections, I’ll schedule calendar blocks and share the runbook link + Grafana dashboard by EOD Tue.

Thanks,
Ben
